headline_marked: [[NASA updates Moon lander plans]], solves long-festering Orion issue for Artemis Program
headline: NASA updates Moon lander plans, solves long-festering Orion issue for Artemis Program
summary: NASA's revised Artemis plan has SpaceX's Starship docking with Orion in high-Earth orbit, while Blue Origin's architecture uses four New Glenn launches and no in-space refueling for initial missions.
details: During a lengthy news conference, NASA provided a detailed overview of how it plans to return astronauts to the lunar surface as soon as 2028 as part of its Artemis Program. This marked the first time NASA has laid out these plans in detail and acknowledged substantial changes in the architecture.

For SpaceX’s Starship vehicle, the revised plan calls for the Orion spacecraft to dock with the Starship lunar lander in high-Earth orbit before transiting to the Moon. This change removes the previous requirement to dock in a near-rectilinear halo orbit, which required more energy and presented difficulties.

For Blue Origin, the mission architecture includes four launches of the New Glenn rocket, but no spacecraft-to-spacecraft refuelings for initial missions. Their plan involves launching three transfer stages to low-Earth orbit, then launching the Blue Moon Mark 2 lander to rendezvous with these stages.

NASA officials continue to anticipate launching the Artemis III mission—a demonstration involving docking with both Blue Moon and Starship near Earth—by "summer" 2027. They are still tracking toward a 2028 launch of Artemis IV, which would involve an actual landing on the lunar surface.

A key question surrounding SpaceX’s architecture is the number of refuelings required to top off a Starship for a lunar mission. A NASA Safety Panel reported "about 22" tanker launches, though Elon Musk claims the actual number will be "six to eight" for the "ultimate potential end state" of Starship.

Additionally, the Blue Origin plans allow for the possibility of its Blue Moon lander rendezvousing with Orion in low-Lunar orbit. This option, a few hundred kilometers above the Moon, would significantly reduce the propellant needed compared to docking in an elliptical lunar orbit.

headline_marked: [[Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra and Pro batteries pictured]] for the first time, hinting at larger capacities
headline: Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra and Pro batteries pictured for the first time, hinting at larger capacities
summary: Alleged battery images from a South Korean safety certification suggest the S27 Ultra could feature a 5,700 mAh battery and the S27 Pro a 5,200 mAh cell, a notable upgrade from previous models.
details: Alleged battery images for the Samsung Galaxy S27 Ultra and S27 Pro have surfaced from a South Korean safety certification. These images, believed to correspond to the SM-S958 and SM-S957 models, hint at substantial battery capacity upgrades for Samsung's upcoming flagships.

A separate Chinese 3C certification further suggests the S27 Ultra could feature a 5,534 mAh rated cell, translating to a 5,700 mAh typical capacity. The S27 Pro is indicated to have a 5,087 mAh rated cell, or 5,200 mAh typical capacity.

This represents a significant increase, especially for the S27 Ultra, which has stuck to 5,000 mAh in recent premium Galaxy devices. The S27 Pro's 5,200 mAh typical rating is also a clear step up from the Galaxy S26's 4,300 mAh capacity.

The battery packs, manufactured by Zhuhai CosMX Power, appear to use traditional Li-ion chemistry rather than the newer silicon-carbon cells found in some competitor flagships. This explains the modest yet welcome increase, as a rumored 7,000 mAh Ultra battery has not materialized.

Beyond battery, other certifications suggest the S27 series will retain 60W wired charging, unchanged from the Galaxy S26 Ultra. Rumors also point to an overhauled design for the S27 Ultra, potentially adopting a rectangular camera plateau.

Adding to the speculation, reports from a South Korean leaker suggest Samsung might accelerate the launch of the Galaxy S27 flagships. An early January announcement is rumored, moving ahead of the traditional February debut and MWC 2027.
